topic.subject: social
topic.title: How the State government works
topic.scope: MLAs, constituencies, majority, Chief Minister, Governor, legislature vs executive

misconceptions.statement: An MLA is a person who works for the whole state equally.
misconceptions.why: Students often fail to grasp the geographical division of power and assume leaders have universal jurisdiction.
misconceptions.fix: An MLA is elected to represent only the specific area or constituency from which they stood for election.

probe.question: If an MLA is elected from a specific area, can they ignore the problems of people living in another part of the state?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because their job is to look after every single person in the state equally.

misconceptions.statement: The party with the most votes in the entire state automatically forms the government.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the total number of individual votes cast with the number of seats won in the legislature.
misconceptions.fix: A party forms the government only if they win more than half of the total constituencies (seats) in the state.

probe.question: If Party A gets more total votes than Party B, but Party B wins more seats, who forms the government?
probe.wrong_answer: Party A, because they got more votes from the people.

misconceptions.statement: All MLAs are part of the government.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate the entire Legislative Assembly with 'the government' without distinguishing between the ruling party and the opposition.
misconceptions.fix: Only the MLAs belonging to the ruling party (or coalition) who are appointed as ministers form the executive government; the others are part of the legislature but act as opposition.

probe.question: Are the MLAs who sit in the opposition also part of the government?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because they are all elected representatives in the assembly.

misconceptions.statement: The Chief Minister makes all the laws alone.
misconceptions.why: Students often attribute state-level decision-making to a single powerful figure, ignoring the collective process of the assembly.
misconceptions.fix: Laws are debated and passed by the entire Legislative Assembly, not just the Chief Minister.

probe.question: Who is responsible for passing a new law in the state?
probe.wrong_answer: The Chief Minister decides and passes the law.
